governing_equation: u_t + (u.grad)u + grad p = nu*Delta u ; div u = 0

requirements.quote: u_t + (u . grad) u + grad p = nu * Delta u,   div u = 0
the periodic square [0, 2*pi]^2, over t in [0, 0.5]
a `fields` dict with keys `u`, `v`, `p` (each an (N, N) array)
relative L2 error of the velocity (u, v) plus an observed spatial-convergence-order check
the pressure is compared after removing its mean (it is defined up to a constant)
The discrete divergence of the velocity must stay near zero -- this is a hard structural gate

implementation_notes: Incompressible Navier-Stokes, Taylor-Green vortex (an exact solution). Multi-field: solve_pde(N) returns fields={u,v,p}. Scored on relative L2 of the velocity (u,v) plus the observed order of the primary field u; pressure p is compared mean-removed (defined up to a constant). The divergence_norm diagnostic is a HARD GATE -- the discrete div u must stay near zero or the solution fails as a CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION regardless of accuracy, so use a projection / pressure-Poisson scheme. For a masked domain set domain_mask; for a compact-support problem set metric='l1'.
